title: BRACHYOLMIA TYPE 4 WITH MILD EPIPHYSEAL AND METAPHYSEAL CHANGES

relationships.phenotype: BRACHYOLMIA TYPE 4 WITH MILD EPIPHYSEAL AND METAPHYSEAL CHANGES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene (603005) on chromosome 10q23.

checks.claim: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: one patient was homozygous for IVS3+2delT, and the other two were compound heterozygotes for c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19)
checks.explanation: Paper reports homozygous and compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations causing AR brachyolmia; 'type 4' designation is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The PAPSS2 gene is located on chromosome 10q23.
checks.evidence_quote: mapped a gene associated with this dwarfing condition to chromosome 10q23-24, a region syntenic with the locus for the brachymorphic mutation on mouse chromosome 19. We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2
checks.explanation: The abstract places the gene in 10q23-24, which matches the standard location given in the claim.

paragraphs.text: Brachyolmia type 4 is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia. Its main features are short-trunk short stature, platyspondyly and mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses of the long bones. It is caused by deficiency of PAPS synthase-2, which produces the universal sulfate donor 3-prime-phosphoadenosine 5-prime-phosphosulfate (PAPS). Some affected individuals also have a defect in the sulfation of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), with low DHEA sulfate, androgen excess and premature pubarche.

checks.claim: Brachyolmia type 4 is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified PAPSS2 as the disease gene for an AR brachyolmia.
checks.explanation: AR form of brachyolmia, a skeletal dysplasia.

checks.claim: The main features of brachyolmia type 4 include short-trunk short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: The six patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood with normal intelligence and facies.
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: The main features of brachyolmia type 4 include platyspondyly.
checks.evidence_quote: platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces
checks.explanation: The abstract reports platyspondyly.

checks.claim: The main features of brachyolmia type 4 include mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses of the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiographs demonstrated delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees
checks.explanation: The abstract reports delayed epiphyseal ossification and, separately, 'Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen predominantly at hips and knees.'

checks.claim: Brachyolmia type 4 is caused by deficiency of PAPS synthase-2.
checks.evidence_quote: The patients had a homozygous loss of function mutation, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18).
checks.explanation: Loss-of-function PAPSS2 mutations imply PAPS synthase-2 deficiency.

checks.claim: PAPS synthase-2 produces the universal sulfate donor 3-prime-phosphoadenosine 5-prime-phosphosulfate (PAPS).
checks.evidence_quote: ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase catalyses the metabolic activation of inorganic sulfate to PAPS, the universal donor for post-translational protein sulfation in all cell types.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Some individuals with brachyolmia type 4 have a defect in the sulfation of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA).
checks.evidence_quote: compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding human PAPS synthase 2 (PAPSS2) in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: A PAPSS2-deficient patient shows impaired DHEA sulfation, but the abstract does not link this to brachyolmia type 4.

checks.claim: Some individuals with brachyolmia type 4 have low DHEA sulfate.
checks.evidence_quote: in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: The PAPSS2-deficient patient had low DHEAS, but the abstract does not mention brachyolmia.

checks.claim: Some individuals with brachyolmia type 4 have androgen excess.
checks.evidence_quote: These observations indicate that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.
checks.explanation: Androgen excess is linked to PAPSS2 deficiency, but the abstract does not mention brachyolmia.

checks.claim: Some individuals with brachyolmia type 4 have premature pubarche.
checks.evidence_quote: in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels
checks.explanation: The PAPSS2-deficient patient had premature pubarche, but the abstract does not mention brachyolmia.

paragraphs.text: The disorder was first described as spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD), Pakistani type. When PAPSS2 mutations were later found in patients diagnosed with brachyolmia, the phenotype was reclassified within the brachyolmia group.

checks.claim: The disorder now called brachyolmia type 4 was first described as spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD), Pakistani type.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a large inbred kindred from a remote area of Pakistan, comprising eight generations, with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD).
checks.explanation: The disorder is described as a distinct SEMD in a Pakistani kindred, but the abstract never uses the name 'Pakistani type'.

checks.claim: PAPSS2 mutations were later found in patients diagnosed with brachyolmia.
checks.evidence_quote: We further examined three patients with similar brachyolmia phenotypes (two Japanese and a Korean) and also identified loss of function mutations in PAPSS2
checks.explanation: PAPSS2 mutations were found in patients with brachyolmia.

checks.claim: After PAPSS2 mutations were found in brachyolmia patients, the SEMD Pakistani type phenotype was reclassified within the brachyolmia group.
checks.explanation: The abstract only mentions a gradation of phenotypes from brachyolmia to SEMD. It does not mention the Pakistani type or any reclassification; this is absent from the abstract supplied.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large consanguineous Pakistani family with an autosomal recessive spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. Affected members had short stature with a short trunk, bowed lower limbs, enlarged knee joints and kyphoscoliosis. Radiographs showed platyspondyly and mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses.

checks.claim: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large consanguineous Pakistani family with an autosomal recessive spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a large inbred kindred from a remote area of Pakistan, comprising eight generations, with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a large inbred Pakistani kindred, and a separate sentence states that the pedigree suggests autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) had short stature with a short trunk.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical findings included short stature evident at birth
checks.explanation: The abstract reports short stature but does not mention a short trunk.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) had bowed lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: short bowed lower limbs
checks.explanation: The abstract reports bowed lower limbs.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) had enlarged knee joints.
checks.evidence_quote: enlarged knee joints
checks.explanation: The abstract reports enlarged knee joints.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) had kyphoscoliosis.
checks.evidence_quote: kyphoscoliosis
checks.explanation: The abstract reports kyphoscoliosis.

checks.claim: Radiographs of affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) showed platyspondyly.
checks.evidence_quote: platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces
checks.explanation: The radiographs showed platyspondyly.

checks.claim: Radiographs of affected members of the Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) showed mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses.
checks.evidence_quote: Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen predominantly at hips and knees.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports mild metaphyseal abnormalities, and a separate sentence reports delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees.

paragraphs.text: Noordam et al. (2009) reported a girl with premature pubarche and hyperandrogenism. Her DHEA sulfate levels were low despite high DHEA, indicating impaired DHEA sulfation. She also had short stature and a mild spondylodysplasia.

checks.claim: Noordam et al. (2009) reported a girl with premature pubarche.
checks.evidence_quote: in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The girl reported by Noordam et al. (2009) had hyperandrogenism.
checks.evidence_quote: hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: Hyperandrogenism is stated.

checks.claim: The girl reported by Noordam et al. (2009) had low DHEA sulfate levels despite high DHEA levels.
checks.evidence_quote: very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: Low DHEAS is stated. High DHEA is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The low DHEA sulfate despite high DHEA in the girl reported by Noordam et al. (2009) indicated impaired DHEA sulfation.
checks.evidence_quote: very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels. In vitro coincubation of human SULT2A1 and wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins confirmed the inactivating nature of the mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract implies impaired sulfation, but it does not give the high DHEA level on which the claim's reasoning rests.

checks.claim: The girl reported by Noordam et al. (2009) had short stature.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention short stature; it may appear in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The girl reported by Noordam et al. (2009) had a mild spondylodysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention spondylodysplasia or any skeletal finding.

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) reported patients with brachyolmia who had PAPSS2 mutations. Their main features were short-trunk short stature and platyspondyly, and some had mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes.

checks.claim: Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) reported patients with brachyolmia who had PAPSS2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified PAPSS2 as the disease gene for an AR brachyolmia.
checks.explanation: Miyake et al. report brachyolmia patients with PAPSS2 mutations.

checks.claim: The main features of the brachyolmia patients with PAPSS2 mutations reported by Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) were short-trunk short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: The six patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: The main features of the brachyolmia patients with PAPSS2 mutations reported by Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) included platyspondyly.
checks.evidence_quote: Their radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs
checks.explanation: Vertebral changes are described, but the abstract does not use the term platyspondyly.

checks.claim: Some of the brachyolmia patients with PAPSS2 mutations reported by Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) had mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes.
checks.evidence_quote: however, epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the changes were variable; it does not specify 'mild' or say that only some patients had them.

paragraphs.text: Noordam et al. (2009) found that their patient's ability to sulfate DHEA was impaired. As a result, DHEA was diverted toward active androgens, which explained her androgen excess and premature pubarche. Oostdijk et al. (2015) studied further PAPSS2-deficient individuals and heterozygous carriers. They confirmed that PAPSS2 deficiency impairs DHEA sulfation and leads to androgen excess.

checks.claim: Noordam et al. (2009) found that their patient's ability to sulfate DHEA was impaired.
checks.evidence_quote: very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels. In vitro coincubation of human SULT2A1 and wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins confirmed the inactivating nature of the mutations.
checks.explanation: Impaired sulfation is implied by the low DHEAS and the in vitro results, but the abstract does not state it directly for the patient.

checks.claim: In the patient reported by Noordam et al. (2009), impaired DHEA sulfation diverted DHEA toward active androgens.
checks.evidence_quote: converts the androgen precursor DHEA to its inactive sulfate ester, DHEAS [corrected], thereby preventing the conversion of DHEA to an active androgen.
checks.explanation: The mechanism is given in general terms, but the abstract does not explicitly say that DHEA was diverted toward active androgens in this patient.

checks.claim: Diversion of DHEA toward active androgens explained the androgen excess and premature pubarche in the patient reported by Noordam et al. (2009).
checks.evidence_quote: These observations indicate that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.
checks.explanation: The abstract concludes that PAPSS2 deficiency causes androgen excess. It does not explicitly use DHEA diversion to explain the pubarche.

checks.claim: Oostdijk et al. (2015) studied further PAPSS2-deficient individuals and heterozygous PAPSS2 carriers.
checks.explanation: This claim is about Oostdijk et al. (2015), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Oostdijk et al. (2015) confirmed that PAPSS2 deficiency impairs DHEA sulfation and leads to androgen excess.
checks.explanation: This claim is about Oostdijk et al. (2015), which this paper does not address.

paragraphs.text: The consanguineous Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Later reports of homozygous and compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations confirmed this pattern.

checks.claim: The consanguineous Pakistani family reported by Ahmad et al. (1998) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of the pedigree strongly suggests autosomal recessive inheritance, and consanguineous loops could account for all the affected individuals being homozygous for the abnormal allele.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the pedigree suggests autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Later reports of homozygous and compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance of the disorder.
checks.explanation: This 1998 abstract does not mention later PAPSS2 mutation reports.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) mapped the disorder in the Pakistani family to chromosome 10q23-q24 by linkage analysis.

checks.claim: Ahmad et al. (1998) mapped the disorder in the Pakistani family to chromosome 10q23-q24 by linkage analysis.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions no linkage analysis and no mapping to 10q23-q24. If this is in the full text, the abstract alone does not show it.

paragraphs.text: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) studied the Pakistani family originally reported by Ahmad et al. (1998). In affected members they found a homozygous nonsense mutation in PAPSS2, which lies in the linked region. In the same study, they showed that the brachymorphic (bm) mouse carries a missense mutation in the orthologous Papss2 gene.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) studied the Pakistani family originally reported by Ahmad et al. (1998).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention Ahmad et al. (1998) or any earlier report of the family.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) found a homozygous nonsense mutation in PAPSS2 in affected members of the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: We characterized a nonsense mutation in ATPSK2 in the SEMD family
checks.explanation: A nonsense mutation is reported, but the abstract does not say it is homozygous.

checks.claim: The PAPSS2 gene lies in the region linked to the disorder in the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: mapped a gene associated with this dwarfing condition to chromosome 10q23-24, a region syntenic with the locus for the brachymorphic mutation on mouse chromosome 19. We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues in the respective regions
checks.explanation: The abstract states that ATPSK2 lies in the mapped region.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) showed that the brachymorphic (bm) mouse carries a missense mutation in the orthologous Papss2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: In the girl with premature pubarche and spondylodysplasia, Noordam et al. (2009) found compound heterozygous inactivating mutations in PAPSS2.

checks.claim: Noordam et al. (2009) found compound heterozygous inactivating mutations in PAPSS2 in the girl with premature pubarche and spondylodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding human PAPS synthase 2 (PAPSS2) in a girl with premature pubarche

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) and Iida et al. (2013) found biallelic PAPSS2 mutations in patients with brachyolmia.

paragraphs.text: The brachymorphic (bm) mouse is an autosomal recessive mutant with short limbs, a short tail and undersulfated cartilage proteoglycans. Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) showed that it carries a missense mutation in Papss2, the mouse ortholog of the human disease gene.

checks.explanation: The abstract does not say how the bm mouse mutation is inherited.

checks.claim: The brachymorphic (bm) mouse has short limbs.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe the mouse having short limbs. It only refers to a cartilage-specific phenotype.

checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention a short tail.

checks.claim: The brachymorphic (bm) mouse has undersulfated cartilage proteoglycans.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention undersulfated cartilage proteoglycans in the mouse.

checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Mouse Papss2 is the ortholog of the human PAPSS2 disease gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues in the respective regions of the human and mouse genomes.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the two genes are orthologues.
